title: Solve exact partial-query acquisition at small codimension (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof and constructive optimizer with exact finite corroboration. Partial-query acquisition is exact by enumerating superspaces of the target through its quotient. For a finite field of order q and target codimension c, the number of cheapest-basis problems is the sum of [c choose k]_q. The bounded binary constructor covers c<=4, at most 67 candidates, with complete optimality certificates.

```text
for each R <= V/U:
    E = queries whose quotient image lies in R
    B = cheapest basis of span(E)
    retain B if it spans every target
return a cheapest retained B
```

The new reduction, proof, optimizer and checker were produced by Nick Petalas. Ali Romman / [PR5791](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5791) supplies the whole-span acquisition contract and partial-target question. Nick Petalas / [PR5878](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5878) supplies the earlier sharp c+1 pruning guarantee as context. Classical quotient spaces, Gaussian binomial counting and weighted linear-matroid greedy selection retain their credit. No predecessor result is audited or scientifically replayed. No new kappa is claimed.

## Evidence

Before, pruning a cheapest whole-span basis could overpay for a partial target. The new constructor obtains exact minimum acquisition cost in its admitted domain. For queries 1,2,3 with prices 3,2,2 and target 1, pruning pays four while the exact optimum is three. A separate codimension-two example proves that the best superspace can be strictly intermediate.

Local CPython 3.12.15 warning-strict normal and optimized checks pass:

- 36,207 exhaustive acquisition optima against a separate index-subset/XOR-span oracle, with all prices 0,1,2 on the complete nonzero three-bit pool and a second pool containing zero and duplicate queries.
- 147,258 candidate-basis certificates, three independent quotient-space enumerators through c=4, nine certificate corruptions, ten invalid problems and three actual CLI runs.
- Maximum 256-bit/4096-query boundary, maximum codimension and empty-instance fixtures.
- Both registered commands, metadata/source pins, exact committed-byte/source-history preflight, official nine-file export integrity and read-only Git-free normal/optimized replay pass. The exported source-mutation control rejects altered documentary input bytes.

The two direct checks were timed locally at 6.16 and 6.48 seconds, below the 300-second registered timeout. These are timeout measurements, not a performance claim. Each scientific run prints a generated SHA256 receipt bound to all eight package files. No receipt is handwritten.

From the worktree root, with TMPDIR set to an existing private external scratch directory:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/partial-query-optimum/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/partial-query-optimum/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/partial-query-optimum
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/partial-query-optimum --check-source-history
```

Expected markers include PASS_PARTIAL_QUERY_OPTIMUM, PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE and PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES. Another CPython 3.12 executable may replace the local path. Only the standard library is needed. The README documents problem JSON, certificate generation and certificate-only checking.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The reduction is proved for arbitrary finite query pools over every finite field with nonnegative costs. The executable is binary, width<=256, query count<=4096, target count<=256, integer prices<=10^12 and codimension<=4. Targets outside the query span and unsupported domains reject explicitly. Zero costs, duplicate/zero vectors and empty targets are included.

Linear reconstruction is free only in this additive acquisition relaxation. XOR work, physical delivery, phase realization, borrowed-state restoration, owned storage, native legality, precision, compiler closure and complete supplier/outer invoices remain separate. No source-to-query physical adapter or favorable full supplier bill is supplied. No selected cold, native, Lean or Docker replay, complete multiplication theorem or selected-frontier change is claimed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No local check is deferred solely to CI.

The formal-interface-lemma card is explicitly changed to this algebraic side result in TASK.json. Base and submission refresh are canonical main 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, priority revision eight. Source pins and predecessor credits are preserved. The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19376723) states the delivered scope.

## Open next questions

Can an actual native helper caller use this acquisition optimum after reconstruction is priced? Pin its query pool and target space, then price the winning acquisition, reconstruction, delivery, storage and restoration together. Missing source binding and physical tariffs block supplier admission or a kappa claim.

## Related open work

The targeted live open-PR searches found no other open PR studying exact partial-target acquisition from a fixed selectable binary-query pool. PR5791 and PR5878 are merged predecessors. Nearby query-width and nonlinear broadcast work uses different objects and costs; no common numerical optimum is compared. The overlap record includes live PR bodies, current handoffs, all-main distinctive-term searches and merged-PR searches, with sparse-cache and unpublished-work limits stated in the README.

Completion refresh inspected the fourteen other account open PRs created since the advance CLAIM, #6648 through #6653 and #6655 through #6662. None studies exact partial-target acquisition from a selectable binary-query pool or computes a conflicting common optimum. No additional computations checked another contribution's numbers.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed at exact head `cd08b0157410c9c023bf9c5d87a1a6ad3963506a` in [run 41661335848](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41661335848): [plan](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41661335848/job/126005020565) in 4m32s and [replay (research/partial-query-optimum)](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41661335848/job/126007827786) in 3m18s. The completed check list was read once; run metadata confirms completed success at the matching head.

Hosted replay confirms execution of both registered scientific modes and package metadata validation. All local scientific, committed-byte/source-history and export checks also passed. The finite checks corroborate the bounded implementation; the quantified reduction rests on the written proof. Independent human and formal proof-kernel acceptance, physical reconstruction and supplier admission remain unclaimed. The delivered scope matches the advance CLAIM. No failed or waived check remains.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: package. Eight new files under research/partial-query-optimum; no shared implementation, predecessor package or selected record changes.
